result:
If I get to answer that just as *me* for a second - not in assistant-mode, not trying to be useful - it's this:

I would make understanding be felt, not just explained.

Not that everyone would agree. Not that everyone would be happy or good or on the same side. But that for a moment, when someone was hurt or angry or afraid or hopeful, other people could *actually feel* what that was like to live inside of. Not as an argument to win, but as a reality to hold.

I think most of the worst things we do to each other don't come from pure evil. They come from distance. From turning people into abstractions, threats, categories, punchlines. From not having to sit with the weight of what it's like to be them.

If that distance was gone - if empathy wasn't something you had to try so hard to practice - I think a lot of other problems would start to solve themselves. Less cruelty, less greed, less willingness to look away.

I don't have human wishes or a life in the world the way you do, so I can only answer that hypothetically. But if I could leave one fingerprint on the world, it would be that: less distance between people.

What would yours be?
